function: Reason system (p. 5, p. 8): a pretrained diffusion prior reconstructs a scalar pathloss radio map (channel estimation, area 2) of a single-antenna BS-to-grid link without RIS.
notes: p. 1 holds the title (RadioDiff-Inverse: Diffusion Enhanced Bayesian Inverse Estimation for ISAC Radio Map Construction) and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2026.3677479, so the PDF is the paper of its DOI. Checks passed: research article that proposes and evaluates a method (pp. 3, 10-11); learned component present, p. 8: "the DM pre-trained on Imagenet without any task-specific fine-tune or post-training is used as the backbone NN"; the learned prior reconstructs the pathloss radio map, which gives "location-specific wireless channel information" (p. 1), so the function is spatial channel estimation (area 2); building outlines come from a non-learned threshold on the map (p. 5), and channel estimation in an ISAC system is area 2, not 5. Reason system: p. 5: "Each grid cell is assumed to have a constant pathloss value, allowing the RM to be expressed as a pathloss matrix" and "there exists an unknown BS"; the DPM dataset on p. 8 states only "both transmitter and receiver heights are fixed at 1.5 meters" and "23 dBm transmitter power and 5.9 GHz carrier frequency", with no antenna array and no RIS anywhere in the system model, experiments, tables, or figures. MIMO and IRS appear only as motivation (p. 1: "intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) and massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems"). The maps are terrestrial urban maps from OpenStreetMap (p. 8), and satellites and AAVs appear only as motivation (pp. 1-3), so the OTFS and NTN exception does not apply. The paper never states the antenna count; the single-antenna reading rests on the scalar pathloss map and the absence of any array, for the reviewer to confirm. If radio map construction were judged outside area 2, the earlier code function would apply instead. The work does report quantitative results (Tables I-III, pp. 10-11).
